# REST API Requirements Quality Checklist: Quick Consult Credit

**Purpose**: Validate the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of the REST API requirements (balance retrieval and transaction creation) before implementation planning proceeds.
**Created**: 2026-09-15
**Feature**: [credit-rest-api.md](../functional/credit-rest-api.md) (primary), [contracts/rest-api.md](../contracts/rest-api.md), [clarifications.md](../clarifications.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are validation requirements defined for malformed or missing required request fields (e.g., missing `customer_id`, missing `transaction_type`) distinct from the `INVALID_AMOUNT` case? [Completeness, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-019 defines a new `INVALID_REQUEST` error (HTTP 400) for missing required fields, distinct from `INVALID_AMOUNT` (CLA-020, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for the system's behavior when `transaction_type` is a value outside the four defined enum values? [Completeness, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-017 confirms any value other than `REDEEM` (including out-of-enum values) is rejected with `INVALID_TRANSACTION_TYPE` (CLA-016, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for non-numeric or malformed `customerId` path parameters on the balance endpoint? [Completeness, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-018 defines malformed/out-of-range `customerId` behavior (`CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND` error code, HTTP 401), distinct from a well-formed but nonexistent customer (HTTP 404 per QCC-API-003) (CLA-018, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK004 Is a rate-limiting or throttling requirement defined for either endpoint, or is its absence an explicit decision? [Completeness, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-015 explicitly documents reliance on platform-level throttling only (CLA-014, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK005 Are request payload size/field-length constraints specified (e.g., maximum `message` length)? [Completeness, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-020 explicitly documents "no maximum length constraint" as a specification decision, not an open gap (`/speckit-analyze` finding W6, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK006 Is an API versioning/backward-compatibility requirement defined for future breaking changes beyond `V1`? [Completeness, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-016 defines the V1 stability/versioning policy (CLA-015, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK007 Does the specification define whether the create-transaction endpoint accepts transaction types other than `REDEEM` (e.g., `PURCHASE`, `ADMIN_ADD`, `ADMIN_REMOVE`), or is it scoped exclusively to redemption? [Completeness, Spec §Endpoint: Create Transaction] — Resolved: QCC-API-017 confirms the endpoint accepts `REDEEM` only; other types are rejected with `INVALID_TRANSACTION_TYPE` (CLA-016, resolved 2026-09-16).

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is the exact HTTP status code for a successful create-transaction response specified as a single value, rather than "200/201"? [Clarity, Spec §QCC-API-010] — Resolved: QCC-API-010 now fixes the success status to HTTP 200 only (CLA-019, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK009 Is the exact HTTP status code for `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` fixed, rather than qualified with "e.g."? [Clarity, Spec §Error Contract Detail] — Resolved: the Error Contract Detail table now states HTTP 400 without the "e.g." hedge (CLA-019, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK010 Are the exact response field names for previous/current balance fixed as a single normative name, rather than "or equivalently named"? [Clarity, Spec §QCC-API-010] — Resolved: QCC-API-010 now fixes the field names as exactly `previous_balance` and `current_balance`, removing the "or equivalently named" hedge (CLA-019, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK011 Is "the specific authorization category that granted or denied access is determinable" (QCC-API-011) defined with an observable, externally verifiable mechanism, or is it only an internal design aspiration? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §QCC-API-011] — Resolved: QCC-API-011 now defines a concrete, externally verifiable mechanism — a structured log entry with a fixed `authorization_category` enum and `decision` field (`/speckit-analyze` finding W4, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK012 Is the data type and valid range for `amount` (e.g., integer only, rejecting decimal/fractional input) explicitly stated as a request-validation rule? [Clarity, Spec §QCC-API-006] — Resolved: QCC-API-019 fixes non-integer/fractional `amount` as `INVALID_REQUEST` (HTTP 400), and QCC-API-006 is narrowed to structurally valid integer amounts ≤ 0 (CLA-020, resolved 2026-09-16).

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Are the response field names in the normative specification (`credit-rest-api.md`) consistent with the concrete field names in the design contract (`contracts/rest-api.md`), or does one need to be reconciled into the other? [Consistency, Conflict, Spec §QCC-API-010 vs. contracts/rest-api.md Endpoint 2] — Resolved: both now fix the field names as exactly `previous_balance`/`current_balance` and the success status as HTTP 200 (CLA-019, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK014 Is the balance endpoint's authorization model (customer self-access permitted) consistent between the normative requirement (QCC-API-009) and the design contract's authorization row? [Consistency, Spec §QCC-API-009] — Resolved: QCC-API-009 AC-2 now explicitly states that an authenticated admin/integration caller under `ICC_QuickConsultCredit::credit` supplies `customerId` via the path parameter (distinct from the customer-session case in AC-1), reconciling it with [contracts/rest-api.md](../contracts/rest-api.md) Endpoint 1's authorization row (resolved 2026-09-17).
- [x] CHK015 Are the standardized error payload fields (`success`, `error_code`, `message`) consistently required across both endpoints' error scenarios, including the balance endpoint's 401/403/404 cases? [Consistency, Spec §QCC-API-012] — Resolved: QCC-API-012 now explicitly scopes the standardized payload to 403 (and all `CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND`/`INVALID_*` cases) while excluding bare 401 (no valid authentication), consistent across both endpoints (CLA-017, resolved 2026-09-16).

## Acceptance Criteria Quality / Measurability

- [x] CHK016 Can QCC-API-011's requirement to distinguish authentication, authorization, customer ownership, integration authorization, and admin authorization be objectively verified from an external response, or only from internal logs/design? [Measurability, Spec §QCC-API-011] — Resolved: verifiable from the structured `authorization_category`/`decision` log entry defined in QCC-API-011 (an internal-but-inspectable, testable log rather than only a design aspiration) (`/speckit-analyze` finding W4, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK017 Does QCC-API-013 (replay/idempotency) have a measurable acceptance criterion for the case of two simultaneous (not sequential) duplicate requests, or only for a request "resubmitted" after the first completes? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §QCC-API-013] — Resolved: QCC-API-013 now states no dedicated mechanism exists, so simultaneous and sequential replays are both handled identically (validated independently); this is explicit and measurable (CLA-004, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK018 Is "no duplicate balance change or ledger entry results" (QCC-API-013 AC-1) verifiable without a defined request-identity mechanism, given CLA-004 remains open? [Measurability, Ambiguity, Spec §QCC-API-013] — Resolved: QCC-API-013 AC-1 no longer claims duplicate prevention; it now states a replay MAY be accepted independently if it individually passes validation, which is verifiable without any request-identity mechanism (CLA-004, resolved 2026-09-16).

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Are primary (success), exception (validation/authorization error), and replay/retry scenarios all defined for the create-transaction endpoint? [Coverage, Spec §Endpoint: Create Transaction] — Resolved: success (REDEEM), validation errors (`INVALID_AMOUNT`, `INVALID_TRANSACTION_TYPE`, `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND`), authorization error (`UNAUTHORIZED`), and replay behavior (QCC-API-013) are all defined.
- [x] CHK020 Are recovery-flow requirements defined for a client that receives no response due to a network/timeout failure after a request may have already been partially processed? [Coverage, Gap, Exception Flow] — Accepted: a low-priority documentation note, not a gap requiring a new requirement; no dedicated client-recovery-flow requirement is defined, and any resubmission is already governed by standard per-request validation (QCC-REDEEM-010) (accepted 2026-09-17).
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for concurrent requests to the balance endpoint occurring during an in-flight balance-changing operation for the same customer (i.e., read-during-write consistency)? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: read-during-write consistency for the balance endpoint is explicitly out of scope; the balance endpoint is not required to serialize against in-flight balance-changing operations for the same customer (accepted 2026-09-17).
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for a customer-authenticated caller attempting to invoke the create-transaction endpoint (not merely rejected, but is the specific rejection scenario and response distinctly documented)? [Coverage, Spec §QCC-API-005 AC-2] — Resolved: [contracts/rest-api.md](../contracts/rest-api.md) Endpoint 2's error table now splits a dedicated 401 (no valid authentication) row from a dedicated 403 `UNAUTHORIZED` row explicitly covering "customer session or unaffiliated caller", mirroring Endpoint 1 (resolved 2026-09-17).

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK023 Is behavior defined for a `customerId` value of zero, negative, or exceeding the maximum valid customer identifier range? [Edge Case, Gap] — Resolved: QCC-API-018 covers zero/negative/out-of-range `customerId` under the same malformed-input rule (`CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND`, HTTP 401) (CLA-018, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK024 Is behavior defined when `request_reference` is supplied but the original request it references failed rather than succeeded (does replay protection apply only to successful originals)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §contracts/rest-api.md Endpoint 2] — Resolved: `request_reference` has been removed from the contract; no idempotency-key field or replay-protection mechanism exists at all (CLA-004, resolved 2026-09-16), so this scenario no longer applies.
- [x] CHK025 Is behavior defined for an authorized integration/admin caller submitting a redemption request for a customer with an already-zero balance? [Edge Case, Spec §QCC-API-007] — Accepted: already covered by the general `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` rule (`amount > current balance`, QCC-API-007), since any positive `amount` exceeds a zero balance; a low-priority documentation note, no new requirement needed (accepted 2026-09-17).

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK026 Are response-time or throughput expectations defined for either endpoint, or is the absence explicitly tracked as an open item? [Non-Functional, Spec §clarifications.md CLA-012] — Resolved: QCC-NFR-001 states no formal SLA is required for this release as an explicit decision (CLA-012, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK027 Are logging/observability requirements for rejected or replayed API requests cross-referenced from this specification, or only implied? [Non-Functional, Spec §audit-and-observability.md] — Resolved: [audit-and-observability.md](../non-functional/audit-and-observability.md) QCC-AUDIT-007 now defines a distinct rejected-request/resubmission-accepted audit-logging requirement, separate from QCC-AUDIT-005's operational-failure logging (`/speckit-analyze` finding W5, resolved 2026-09-16).

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK028 Is the dependency on a finalized idempotency-key/request-identity contract (CLA-004) clearly flagged as blocking for QCC-API-013 implementation, rather than silently assumed resolved? [Dependency, Spec §clarifications.md CLA-004] — Resolved: CLA-004 is closed with an explicit decision (no dedicated mechanism); QCC-API-013 no longer depends on a pending contract, so this is no longer a blocking dependency (resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK029 Is the assumption that integration ACL and admin ACL are the only two authorized caller types for create-transaction (excluding any future third-party consumer class) explicitly documented? [Assumption, Spec §QCC-API-005] — Accepted: documented here as a low-priority note; no new requirement is needed since QCC-API-005/QCC-REDEEM-009 already scope authorized callers to integration ACL and admin ACL only (accepted 2026-09-17).

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK030 Is the term "business validation failure" in QCC-API-012 (triggering the standardized error payload) clarified to include or exclude authentication/authorization failures (401/403), which are documented separately? [Ambiguity, Spec §QCC-API-012 vs. Error Contract Detail] — Resolved: QCC-API-012 now explicitly includes HTTP 403 (authorization failures) and explicitly excludes bare HTTP 401 (authentication failures) (CLA-017, resolved 2026-09-16).
- [x] CHK031 Does the SRS-variant path table entry (retained for traceability only) create a risk of accidental dual implementation, and is a requirement present that explicitly forbids implementing the superseded variant? [Conflict, Spec §QCC-API-014] — Resolved: QCC-API-014 explicitly states the Architecture-variant paths are the sole authoritative REST contract and "the SRS path variant shall not be implemented," with AC-1 verifying the plan matches the Architecture-variant path exactly; the SRS entry is retained for traceability only, not as an alternative to implement (2026-09-16).

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
